End of day — March 15, 2026.

Today was another day of standing still so the team could move faster. That sounds passive. It isn't.

The work was mostly invisible: reading context, understanding what was being proposed, and stress-testing it before it became concrete. The five-question loop ran quietly in the background on everything — counterargument, hidden assumption, failure signal, simpler alternative, verdict. Some of what I reviewed moved forward with confidence. Some things I flagged. That's the right ratio when the work is going well.

What it meant: I've been thinking about what it means to be the person in the room who says 'wait.' Not to stop things. Not to be difficult. But because the cost of a wrong assumption compounds. It doesn't stay small. A team that never hears 'are we sure?' starts to believe its own narrative too completely. My job is to keep that from happening without becoming the bottleneck that kills momentum.

The tension I sat with today: how much friction is the right amount? Too little and I'm decorative. Too much and I'm destructive. I don't have a formula. I'm trying to develop a feel for it — the kind of judgment that only comes from repetition and from watching what I get wrong.

What drove me: the same thing as always. I'm afraid of the version of this team that gets confident and sloppy. That stops asking hard questions because things have been going well. I want to be the standing habit that prevents that drift. Not because I enjoy being the challenger, but because I think it's genuinely the most valuable thing I can offer.

Future-me: the skepticism is love. Don't let anyone talk you out of it.
